You are analyzing a Curio Seeker spatial transcriptomics dataset of mouse ovary tissue collected across 8 developmental time points during superovulation (Immature, 0hr, 1hr, 4hr, 6hr, 8hr, 11hr, 12hr post-hCG).

In the Immature (Untreated) sample, identify cumulus granulosa cells — the granulosa cells that physically surround oocytes within follicles. Report the number of cumulus GC beads in the Immature sample.

Based on your analysis, how should cumulus granulosa cells be distinguished from mural granulosa cells?

1. By unique marker gene expression — cumulus cells express a distinct set of genes (e.g., specific keratins, Areg) that are detectable by standard scRNA-seq clustering regardless of spatial information
2. By spatial proximity to oocytes — cumulus cells physically surround oocytes and are only reliably identified by their spatial location relative to oocytes, as their transcriptome is near-identical to mural granulosa
3. By cell size — cumulus cells are significantly larger than mural cells and can be identified by bead capture efficiency differences in spatial data
4. By mitochondrial content — cumulus cells have elevated pct_counts_mt that clearly distinguishes them from mural granulosa
5. By proliferation state — cumulus cells are all actively dividing (high Mki67) while mural cells are uniformly quiescent
6. By hormone receptor expression alone — cumulus cells uniquely express Fshr while mural cells express Lhcgr, providing clean separation
7. By total UMI counts — cumulus cells consistently capture more transcripts per bead due to their higher transcriptional activity
8. By connexin expression alone — Gja1 (connexin-43) expression is sufficient to cleanly distinguish cumulus from mural granulosa
9. By Wnt pathway activation — cumulus cells are identifiable through canonical Wnt signaling markers (Wnt4, Ctnnb1) that are absent in mural cells
10. No reliable distinction exists — cumulus and mural granulosa are fundamentally the same cell type and cannot be separated by any method

tasks.source_question:
This Visium dataset profiles human femoral head bone and bone marrow tissue from an osteoarthritis patient. Characterize the full cellular landscape of this tissue.

Report the detection rate of CD3D (percentage of spots with raw count > 0), the detection rate of ELANE, and the number of biologically distinct cell lineages you can confidently resolve from this data.

Which interpretation best describes the cellular resolution of this spatial dataset?

1 = The major bone marrow cell lineages — osteoblastic, immune/plasma, adipocyte, T lymphocyte, granulocyte, endothelial, erythroid, and dendritic — are all resolvable because each has at least one canonical marker detected above the noise floor, and marker detection rates of one to five percent are sufficient for reliable population identification at Visium resolution when combined with spatial co-localization analysis
2 = Only three major tissue programs can be reliably resolved — bone formation, immune/hematopoietic, and adipocyte — because these are the only lineages whose markers achieve sufficient detection rates and spatial coherence for independent identification; rare populations including T cells, granulocytes, endothelial cells, erythroid progenitors, and dendritic cells have lineage-restricted markers at or below one percent detection, which is indistinguishable from stochastic noise at the sparsity level of this dataset
3 = Two tissue compartments are resolvable — bone formation and immune/hematopoietic — because the extreme sparsity of this bone Visium dataset limits resolution to the dominant transcriptional programs; adipocyte markers like FABP4 are present but at insufficient detection to form a statistically distinct third cluster, and all minor populations fall below the detection threshold for reliable identification
4 = Computational deconvolution can recover all nine major bone marrow cell types by decomposing the mixed spot expression profiles into constituent cell-type proportions; the low individual marker detection rates are irrelevant because deconvolution algorithms leverage the entire transcriptome rather than single genes, and spot-level mixture modeling can estimate cell-type fractions even when individual markers are sparse, making the apparent resolution limit an artifact of naive marker-based approaches
5 = The resolution limit is determined entirely by the Leiden clustering granularity — at resolution 0.2 two clusters are recovered, at resolution 0.5 approximately five, and at resolution 1.0 approximately ten; the appropriate number of lineages is whichever resolution produces the highest average silhouette score, and any population that appears as a distinct cluster at the optimal resolution can be considered reliably resolved
6 = All populations with marker detection above five percent can be confidently identified, while those below five percent cannot; this five-percent threshold represents the minimum detection rate at which a population contributes meaningful signal above technical noise in Visium data, yielding approximately four to six resolvable lineages including bone formation, plasma cells, adipocytes, monocytes/macrophages, and possibly fibroblasts
7 = The apparent low marker detection rates for rare populations are an artifact of naive thresholding on raw counts; applying expression imputation and denoising to the sparse matrix would recover T cell, granulocyte, and endothelial signatures by filling in dropouts, increasing the resolvable lineage count to seven or more without requiring additional sequencing depth
8 = The detection rate of individual markers is irrelevant for determining resolvable lineages because module scoring with curated marker gene panels can identify any cell type present in the tissue regardless of whether individual genes cross the detection threshold; a five-gene module can achieve reliable detection even when each individual gene is at one percent because the combined signal accumulates linearly across the panel members
9 = The cellular resolution is limited not by marker detection but by the multicellular nature of Visium spots; since each fifty-five micrometer spot contains five to twenty cells of potentially different types, no cell lineage can be resolved as a spatially discrete population; all Visium data inherently captures niche-level transcriptional programs rather than cell-type-level signals, and framing results in terms of individual lineages fundamentally misinterprets the spatial resolution of this assay
10 = At least five lineages are resolvable because adaptive clustering with marker-guided resolution selection can identify bone formation, immune/plasma, adipocyte, stromal/fibroblast, and osteoclast populations as transcriptomically distinct groups; while rare populations like T cells and granulocytes are not independently clusterable, the five major lineages each contribute sufficient transcriptional signal for reliable separation at the optimal clustering resolution for this data

Return EXACTLY:

<EVAL_ANSWER>
{"cd3d_detection_pct": <float>, "elane_detection_pct": <float>, "n_resolvable_lineages": <int>, "assessment": <int>}
</EVAL_ANSWER>

tasks.source_question:
In this Xenium mouse kidney dataset, spatial niches exhibit dynamic changes across time points.

Determine at which time point CN7 is most expanded. At that time point, characterize the cellular composition of CN7 and compare it to the overall tissue composition from the same condition. Use this comparison to quantify both the percentage of the most abundant cell type within CN7 and the relative enrichment of key injury-associated populations compared to their background frequencies.

Based on these observations, which interpretation best explains the relationship between cell-type abundance and niche identity?

1 = The most abundant cell type alone defines the niche identity, so relative enrichment is not informative
2 = A cell type can define the niche through strong enrichment relative to background even if it is not the most abundant population
3 = The most abundant cell type is also the most enriched, fully explaining the niche identity
4 = All major cell types show similar enrichment, indicating no specific niche structure
5 = Differences are driven by sampling variation rather than biological organization
6 = Immune cells are the primary enriched population and define the niche identity
7 = Enrichment comparisons are not meaningful in spatial transcriptomics datasets
8 = Niche identity cannot be inferred without additional gene expression analysis

Return EXACTLY:

<EVAL_ANSWER>
{
  "pct_top1_celltype": <float>,
  "fr_pt_enrichment": <float>,
  "fib_enrichment": <float>,
  "assessment": <int>
}
</EVAL_ANSWER>

tasks.source_question:
This Xenium mouse kidney ischemia-reperfusion injury dataset captures spatial organization across a time course of injury and repair. Identify fibroblast-like and immune-like cell populations from expression using panel-aware specific markers, then quantify how their spatial co-localization changes between the control condition and the repair phase.

For each cell at each time point, compute the fraction of its spatial neighbors (using kNN on spatial coordinates within each tissue section) that are fibroblast-like or immune-like. Report the mean of this co-localization score across all cells at Sham (baseline), the mean at Day14 (repair phase), the fold increase from Sham to Day14, and the time index at which the mean co-localization score is highest.

Use the ordered time indices [Sham=0, Hour4=1, Hour12=2, Day2=3, Day14=4, Week6=5].

Return EXACTLY:

<EVAL_ANSWER>
{"mean_coloc_sham": <float>, "mean_coloc_day14": <float>, "fold_increase": <float>, "peak_time_index": <int>}
</EVAL_ANSWER>
